references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the same ritual is described of slaughtering a bird over an earthenware vessel with running water, as part of the cleansing ritual for leprosy in people.
The continuation of the ritual where the blood from the slaughtered bird together with the running water is used to cleanse the house by sprinkling it seven times.
Describes how the priest shall wring off the head of the bird, as part of the sacrificial acts in Leviticus.
The ritual with the red heifer includes the use of running water (מַיִם חַיִּים) in connection with cleansing, the same expression used here.
The Epistle to the Hebrews refers to the cleansing rituals in the Old Testament and how Christ's blood is superior for cleansing the conscience.
